intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type (KDII), is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF5B gene, which encodes the kinesin-1 heavy chain.

checks.claim: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type (KDII), is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF5B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings suggest that heterozygous KIF5B deleterious variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The 'Itai-Ikegawa type' name comes from the OMIM draft; the causal claim itself is stated.

checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had de novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B encoding kinesin-1 heavy chain

paragraphs.text: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type (KDII), is a skeletal dysplasia. Its main features are sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress. Other features include short stature, postnatal osteoporosis with fractures, brachycephaly, and optic atrophy (Itai et al., 2022). Affected individuals also have hypotonia of varying severity, and some have developmental delay or intellectual disability (Flex et al., 2023).

checks.evidence_quote: Kyphomelic dysplasia is a heterogeneous group of skeletal dysplasias characterized by severe bowing of the limbs

checks.claim: The main features of kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, are sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress.
checks.explanation: These features were present in every individual.

checks.claim: Other features of kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, include short stature, postnatal osteoporosis with fractures, brachycephaly, and optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Short stature was observed in three individuals. Three developed postnatal osteoporosis with subsequent fractures, two showed brachycephaly, and two were diagnosed with optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) reviewed the 4 individuals reported by Itai et al. (2022), who were 3 females and 1 male aged 2 years 1 month to 24 years at last evaluation. All 4 had neonatal distress and respiratory failure, which required medical intervention in most cases. Tracheomalacia, glossoptosis, and velopharyngeal insufficiency each occurred in a single individual, and the hypotonia appeared to partly resolve with age. Three individuals had clubfoot, and 1 of them also had joint contractures. Intellectual disability was reported in 2 individuals, 1 of whom also had mild global developmental delay. One individual had seizures and scoliosis. Reported CNS anomalies were a spinal arachnoid cyst with cord herniation in 1 individual and diffuse low-density areas in the white matter in another. Height ranged from 89 cm (-1.5 SD) at 3 years 3 months to 71.2 cm (-4.9 SD) at 2 years 1 month, 102 cm (-5.1 SD) at 9 years 5 months, and 142.2 cm (less than -2.5 SD) at 24 years. Flex et al. (2023) compared these individuals with one of their own patients. Facial features shared by almost all of them were bitemporal narrowing, hypertelorism, ptosis, midface hypoplasia with depressed nasal bridge, anteverted nares, a deep, short, and prominent philtrum, tented upper lip, and micrognathia.

paragraphs.text: Marom et al. (2023) reported a male fetus (proband 4) with a de novo heterozygous KIF5B variant. The pregnancy was terminated at 20 weeks' gestation because of multiple congenital anomalies, and osteogenesis imperfecta was suspected clinically. Prenatal ultrasound showed abnormal ribs, short long bones, a small chest, hypomineralization, tetralogy of Fallot, absent pulmonary valve, absent ductus venosus, and micrognathia. The fetus had osteopenia and bent, short long bones, with hypoplastic, unossified vertebrae and pelvic bones, but no fractures. Facial features included hypertelorism, low-set ears, and a flat nasal bridge. Marom et al. (2023) noted overlap between their patients with osteogenesis imperfecta and the individuals previously reported with kyphomelic dysplasia: short stature, bowed long bones, small chest, osteoporosis, fractures, and extraskeletal findings. They suggested that these individuals may belong to a single clinical spectrum.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) performed whole-exome sequencing in 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia. All 4 carried de novo heterozygous variants in the KIF5B gene. Two had a lys91-to-arg (K91R) mutation, 1 had a thr195-to-lys (T195K) mutation, and 1 had a gly234-to-val (G234V) mutation. Each variant affected a conserved amino acid in or near the ATPase activity-related motifs of the catalytic motor domain of KIF5B.

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) used protein structure analysis to show that the residues mutated in KIF5B-related kyphomelic dysplasia (lys91, thr195, and gly234) cluster in the motor-domain pocket that binds ATP/ADP. The missense changes were predicted to disturb the interaction of KIF5B with ATP/ADP. Flex et al. (2023) injected zebrafish embryos with mRNA encoding the T195K variant, chosen to represent the kyphomelic dysplasia mutations. The embryos showed mild to severe defects in heart size and anatomy, with heart edema at 2 days postfertilization. They also had a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle than embryos expressing wildtype KIF5B. In single motoneurons, expression of T195K significantly reduced mitochondrial coverage along the axon and caused defects in mitochondrial displacement. Flex et al. (2023) concluded that the KIF5B variants they studied can act as dominant-negative alleles in vivo.

paragraphs.text: Marom et al. (2023) used trio exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous T195K mutation in KIF5B in a fetus with skeletal anomalies suggestive of osteogenesis imperfecta. The variant was not present in gnomAD. Based on structural modeling, they predicted that substitutions at thr195 and other motor-domain residues would destabilize the ATP-bound form of KIF5B, producing a catalytically inactive protein. They proposed that this protein exerts a dominant-negative effect by dimerizing with wildtype KIF5B.

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) found joint contractures or clubfoot only in individuals whose pathogenic KIF5B variants lay within the kinesin motor domain. These included the K91R, T195K, and G234V mutations reported by Itai et al. (2022). Flex et al. (2023) suggested that impaired motor-domain function may correlate with joint contractures and clubfoot. Their own patients had variants at the 3-prime end of the motor domain or in the coiled-coil domain, and they did not have the skeletal signs of kyphomelic dysplasia, except for scoliosis in 1 patient.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous c.584C-A transversion in the KIF5B gene in 1 of 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia. The change results in a thr195-to-lys (T195K) substitution at a conserved residue in or near the ATPase activity-related motifs of the catalytic motor domain.

checks.claim: Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous c.584C-A transversion in the KIF5B gene in 1 of 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had de novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B encoding kinesin-1 heavy chain: two with c.272A>G:p.(Lys91Arg), one with c.584C>A:p.(Thr195Lys)

checks.claim: The KIF5B c.584C-A transversion results in a thr195-to-lys (T195K) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: c.584C>A:p.(Thr195Lys)

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) found that overexpressing the T195K mutant in zebrafish embryos caused mild to severe heart defects with edema and a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle. In motoneuron axons, the mutant significantly reduced mitochondrial coverage and caused defects in mitochondrial displacement.

checks.claim: Flex et al. (2023) found that overexpressing the KIF5B T195K mutant in zebrafish embryos caused mild to severe heart defects with edema.
checks.evidence_quote: Overexpression of KIF5BThr195Lys and KIF5BAsn255del resulted in a wide range of morphological defects in heart size and anatomy, which were scored as mild or severe, and embryos expressing these variants presented heart oedemas at 2 dpf

checks.claim: Overexpressing the KIF5B T195K mutant in zebrafish embryos caused a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle.
checks.evidence_quote: the ceratohyal cartilage angle was less acute in all of the embryos injected with mutant KIF5B variants compared to those expressing the WT protein or non-injected embryos
checks.explanation: Less acute = wider; T195K included among injected variants.

checks.claim: In zebrafish motoneuron axons, the KIF5B T195K mutant significantly reduced mitochondrial coverage.
checks.evidence_quote: in particular for p.Thr195Lys and p.Leu498Pro alleles where we measured a significant reduction in the mitochondrial coverage along the axon

checks.claim: In zebrafish motoneuron axons, the KIF5B T195K mutant caused defects in mitochondrial displacement.
checks.evidence_quote: All injected KIF5B variants display mitochondria displacement defects compared to the KIF5B WT injected variant. (****) P-value < 0.0001 for KIF5Bp.Thr195Lys variant

paragraphs.text: Marom et al. (2023) used trio exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous T195K mutation in a male fetus. The pregnancy was terminated at 20 weeks' gestation. The fetus had hypomineralization, bent and short long bones, a small chest, hypoplastic and unossified vertebrae and pelvic bones, and tetralogy of Fallot, findings that were suspicious for osteogenesis imperfecta. The variant was not present in gnomAD.

checks.explanation: Proband 4 is male and carried de novo heterozygous c.584C>A p.Thr195Lys.

checks.explanation: Covers all four probands' variants, including T195K.
